paraphrase: Thus have I heard: at one time the Lord dwelt in the 'bhagas of the vajra-women', the heart of the body, speech and mind of all tathāgatas, with countless bodhisattvas (named the samaya-, body-, speech-, mind-vajra and the rest).
notes: Indrabhūti's gloss (quoted in Bhattacharya's note from the Jñānasiddhi) reads 'heart' as gnosis, gnosis as the vajra-woman, and 'bhaga' as that which destroys (bhañj) the afflictions — a non-literal reading recorded as tea:jnanasiddhi:p58.

paraphrase: The practice is divided into service (sevā), near-attainment (upasādhana), attainment (sādhana) and great attainment (mahāsādhana).
notes: Located by the terms sevā/upasādhana in chs. 12 and 18 of the e-text; precise verse not fixed.

paraphrase: The six-limbed yoga is: withdrawal (pratyāhāra), meditation (dhyāna), breath control (prāṇāyāma), retention (dhāraṇā), recollection (anusmṛti) and absorption (samādhi); without this 'service' in six limbs the supreme attainment does not arise.
notes: Quoted exactly, with the e-text's misprints ('dhyānann', 'ucayte' for dhyānaṃ, ucyate). Verse numbers in ch. 18 are the unit's count.

paraphrase: Withdrawal is the ten senses each staying in its own place; meditation is the conception of the five objects of desire as the five buddhas, fivefold (with reasoning, investigation, joy, bliss and one-pointedness); breath control is to draw out the breath — of the five gnoses and five elements — in the form of a ball and imagine it at the tip of the nose as a five-coloured jewel; retention is to meditate one's mantra in the heart and place it in the drop of life-wind, restraining the senses.
notes: Definitions summarized; no method beyond what the verses name.

paraphrase: When the mind has entered the vajra of cessation a sign arises, fivefold: first like a mirage, second like smoke, third like fireflies, fourth blazing like a lamp, fifth constant light like a cloudless sky.

paraphrase: Recollection is to recollect the form one has visualized — there an appearance arises; absorption: gathering all things by the union of wisdom and means and meditating them within the image, the sudden arising of gnosis is called samādhi.

paraphrase: (The bodhicitta taught by the Lord, vajra of body, speech and mind:) in the absence of being there is no meditation; meditation is not meditation; thus being is not being, and meditation is not apprehended.
notes: Third verse of ch. 2 in the unit's count; quoted in the Bodhicittavivaraṇa tradition.

paraphrase: Vairocana's bodhicitta: free of all entities, devoid of aggregates, elements, sense-fields and of grasped and grasper, by the sameness of the selflessness of phenomena one's own mind is primordially unborn, of the nature of emptiness.
notes: Quoted exactly as the e-text reads ('dharmanairātmāsamatayā', understood as dharmanairātmya-).

paraphrase: Chapter 5 ('the conduct') declares that caṇḍālas, bamboo-workers and others intent on killing, and even those who have committed the heinous deeds, succeed in this supreme vehicle, while those who revile their master never succeed; it lists killing, lying, coveting others' wealth, constant desire, the eating of impure substances and sexual transgression with kinswomen as not preventing the non-conceptual practitioner's success. The assembled bodhisattvas are astonished and ask why the Lord speaks such ill words; the tathāgatas reply: 'Do not say so — this is the pure dharmatā of the buddhas who know the essence, arisen from the meaning of the essential dharma: the path of awakening.'
notes: Summarized; only the first verse is quoted. The Ārya commentary (Pradīpoddyotana) reads such verses through the six alternatives (intentional, not literal); recorded here as the text states it.
